messages.content:
Work on the problem using the material actually exposed in this request and your background knowledge. The problem has no supplied answer key or scoring rule. Claims, criticisms and methods are fallible. Do not invent a source, an observation, an earlier event, or a dependency to fill a field. A missing view says what you can currently see; it does not establish what happened earlier. Return a JSON object with exactly two independently authored string fields: body and commitments. Body is your public prose contribution. Commitments says what taking your contribution up would involve. An empty commitment surface is allowed when none can be identified. Do not repeat the body wholesale into commitments.

Use FCL-1 for the commitment surface, encoded as a JSON document inside the commitments string: {"language":"FCL-1","records":[...],"uptake":[...]}. Each record has unique local id, type (claim|commitment|objection|use|problem), and text (unrestricted prose). Optional prose fields: scope, action, consequence, grounds, bearing. Optional arrays of references: target, depends, mentions, revises, withdraws. References are local IDs or exposed-artifact-label#local-ID; do not invent hidden IDs. A commitment proposes a scoped use, action, application or consequence; an objection alleges a defect whose bearing can itself be criticized; a use proposes an uptake or response; a problem states an unresolved question. depends asserts reliance; mentions only locates material. uptake lists the records you currently propose to use, not certified truths. No record type or optional field must be present. Empty records and uptake are allowed. Express uncertainty or an unrepresentable relation in prose rather than inventing a relation. The body remains unrestricted prose.

Return one JSON object with exactly two string fields: "body" and "commitments". Write the actual commitments separately; do not copy the body into that field as a storage shortcut.

# carry

Produce the present account and commitment interface for the next complete template invocation. The material may support a revision, an unresolved problem, or retaining something. Preserve the grounds needed for whatever uptake you propose.

## Original problem (task)
[d31d61f36df18c74] (h005.task.v1)
I share a flat with two friends. We keep arguing about ordinary household chores. Sometimes we agree on who will do something, but later we disagree about what the agreement meant. Our work schedules change, and one friend has started avoiding the conversations. What should I do?

BODY
The three pieces disagree less than they appear to, and the part where they genuinely disagree can be settled cheaply by observation rather than argument. The account's mechanics survive their criticism in repaired form; the objection's two structural points — the single point of failure at the one-to-one, and its asserted-but-unargued priority — converge with the rival's strongest conjecture, that the avoidance may be a verdict on who convenes; and the rival's big reframing, over-coupling, cannot be settled from the description, but its own discriminating checks can be run for free inside a repaired version of the design it rivals. So my resolution: keep the account's core after three repairs, replace its entrance, hold the rival's reordering as a branch rather than a starting point, and run the whole plan explicitly as a probe.

What I use unchanged: the underspecification conjecture and the churn critique, the trial mechanics and the goodwill stance — plus, newly, the objection's two design facts (definitions of done relocate rather than abolish ambiguity; availability-keyed claiming with no-blame misses runs on unverifiable self-report) and the rival's discriminating checks and sequencing principle (decouple what is cheap; explicitness earns its keep on what remains).

Three repairs, all supplied by the objection itself. First, since a one-line definition of done is an incomplete contract in miniature, expect meta-disputes at the line and pre-agree that a contested line is rewritten together rather than adjudicated against past performance — the no-blame rule extended from misses to lines. This drops the account's one over-strong clause ('without any fairness negotiation at all') while keeping what the evidence supports. Second, a ledger-use rule: the shared record is used only openly, at a standing review, by anyone; no private tallies. That dissolves most of the ledger-versus-score-keeping tension, and it answers the objection's sharpest question — what flips absorbed unevenness into raised fairness — with a venue instead of a threshold: raising is routinized as a standing agenda item, so tolerance no longer needs a tripwire. Third, a fairness floor: the revision meeting opens by looking together at claimed and completed totals. That meets the exploitation worry without surveillance and turns the trial's record into the instrument for settling the account's own open question about who does more.

The entrance is where I part from the account. The process-first one-to-one rests on the plan's weakest claim, is itself an instance of the avoided genre, and is the plan's only door. The rival lands on the same spot from the other side: if avoidance is a verdict on the user-as-convener, a better system from the same convener is no remedy. Revised entrance: talk first with the non-avoidant third flatmate — the available, easy conversation — to co-own the proposal; then start the artifact asynchronously and opt-in, opened by one person, joinable without any meeting, carrying an explicit stand-down line ('I don't want to run this — rearrange it freely'), co-signed where possible; reserve the one-to-one until the opt-in window has shown something. The criterion behind this generalizes: with the diagnosis unresolved, buy moves that are useful under every live hypothesis and harmful under none. Process-aversion is met by the format, convener-aversion by the stand-down, overload by the asynchrony, and quiet under-contribution is surfaced by the totals review. The old entrance could not say that; this one can.

Left open, deliberately: the framing contest. Whether this flat has an agreement problem or an over-coupling problem is now the probe's business. The run generates three observations: where disputes recur (at claims, at done-lines, or not at all); whether the avoider engages when nobody convenes them; whether the artifact gets used at all when nobody pushes. The review then branches: continue the mechanics, open the rival's decoupling menu, address fairness from the totals, or hand over convening entirely. Also open: why the friend avoids (the window is evidence), and a noted weakness in the rival's best menu item — domain ownership binds a standard to a person and so inherits the churn objection it was meant to escape, needing scheduled swaps if ever adopted.

Rejected: the rival's stand-down-and-decouple as the fixed first move. It concedes the convener hypothesis before testing it; decoupling decisions themselves need the agreement capacity the rival says is scarce, so the ordering inherits a milder version of the bootstrap problem; and decoupling is less reversible than a two-week opt-in trial. Its components survive — in the entrance and in the held menu — so little is lost. I also decline to rest anything on the charitable reading of avoidance, and decline a numerical fairness trigger in favour of the routinized review.

One new caveat of my own: the entrance assumes the third flatmate is approachable and not part of the problem. If that first conversation shows otherwise — co-avoidance, or that they are the quiet under-contributor — the design falls back to reserved one-to-ones with each friend, no shared artifact until one is secured. And the standing caveat of this whole exchange applies to my synthesis too: none of us can see this flat. The diagnoses are conjectures; the checks are the content. What I would defend unconditionally is the criterion and the probes, not any framing.
